summary: Photoshop-style crop past the image edge: picked-colour fill for the new area (the outpaint target), snapping to image edges, and a RESOLUTION type that takes an exact WxH and is the only type that resamples. No auto-mask by user decision. Started immediately, card opens in doing.
Work started same session as carding.

Code complete, maturity in-progress to validating. Server half PROVEN: unit tests 10/10, Sharp end-to-end on real files, and the live route returning correct sizes with fill outside plus source pixels inside. Trap found and recorded: Sharp applies extend AFTER extraction whatever the call order, so extend and extract must be two passes with a toBuffer between - chaining them throws extract_area bad extract area. Canvas half is UNPROVEN, it needs the app open: drag past the edge, snap feel at 8 screen px, the union-fit zoom and its no-refit-while-dragging rule, and Apply from the panel. Video and App cropTool.js untouched by design.

Round 1 live test: RATIO and FREE good. Three RESOLUTION-path bugs found and FIXED, not yet re-tested. (1) Output Resolution stayed visible in RATIO/FREE - the component CSS sets display:flex on its sections, which beats the UA [hidden] rule; explicit [hidden] rules added. (2) No Apply button when the tool opened in RESOLUTION - setCropSize was missing from the MpiCanvas _methods ALLOWLIST, so el.setCropSize was undefined, _pushShape threw, and everything mounted after that line was gone. (3) The box stopped matching the typed size after a family round-trip - a ratio alone cannot restore an exact box because re-entry re-fits the largest centred box, so the viewer now keeps _activeCropSize. Two source-text regression tests added and mutation-checked. Handoff 9f9913a2 written.

User-verified live, all 8 on-screen checks pass: drag past the edge in all three resolution types, snap feel accepted at 8 screen px, union-fit zoom with no mid-drag refit, dashed source-bounds outline, Apply end to end with the fill colour, fill persisting across a tool swap and a restart, video crop unchanged, and the three round-1 RESOLUTION fixes. Round 2 opened with a FALSE ALARM worth remembering: the reported failures were a stale Electron renderer, not a regression - the app booted at 23:51 and the fixes were written 00:17-00:19, so the running page never fetched them. The console stack said MpiCanvasViewer.js:1101 where the call sits at 1110 on disk; a stack line number that disagrees with the file is a stale build, and comparing file mtimes to the process StartTime settles it in one command. Video/Apps port stays out of scope by user decision - cropTool.js is normalized 0-1 and ffmpeg -vf crop cannot pad, unlike Resize which is a ComfyUI op and got video for free.
